summary: Alexander von Humboldt worked in history and archaeology. He studied at the Universities of Frankfurt (Oder), Göttingen (under Christian Gottlob Heyne and Georg Christoph Lichtenberg), Jena, and TU Bergakademie Freiberg, later holding a post at the University of Jena.

Alexander von Rospatt specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of London and earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He taught at Leipzig University and serves as Professor at UC Berkeley.

A scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology, Alexander von Staël-Holstein studied at Dorpat/Tartu, Berlin, Halle-Wittenberg (under Richard Pischel), and Harvard. He held posts at Saint Petersburg State University, Peking University, Harvard, and directed the Sino-Indian Institute.
Alexandra David-Néel worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Royal Conservatory of Brussels and trained under Philippe-Édouard Foucaux and Kazi Dawa Samdup.
Alexandra van der Geer is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied under Leendert A. van Daalen, Henk Bodewitz, and Paul Y. Sondaar.

Alexandre Langlois was an Indologist who studied under Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. He taught at the Lycée Charlemagne, served as an inspector for the Académie de Paris, and was a member of the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres.

Alexis Sanderson is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Balliol College, Oxford, and under Swami Lakshman Joo. He held fellowships at Merton and Brasenose, served as Lecturer and Professor at Oxford, and was an All Souls Fellow.

Alf Hiltebeitel was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Oakwood Friends School, Haverford College, and the University of Chicago and its Divinity School, before serving on the faculty at George Washington University from 1968 onward.
Alf Sommerfelt was a linguistics scholar who founded the Norwegian Association for Linguistics in 1924 and served as professor of linguistics at the University of Oslo from 1931 to 1962.

Alfons Fürst specializes in religious studies, history/archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the Universities of Tübingen and Regensburg (habilitating under Norbert Brox). He held a post at Bamberg and became Professor and Dean of Catholic Theology at Münster.

Alfonsa Ferrari worked in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Carlo Formichi at Sapienza University of Rome from around 1937 to 1941, continuing there with post-graduate research until approximately 1948.

Alfred Bloom was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned his Ph.D. at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi and held faculty posts at the University of Oregon, University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Alfred Chilton Pearson worked in linguistics and Indology. He was educated at Highgate School and King's College School, and studied under John Peile at Christ's College, University of Cambridge.

Alfred Cooper Woolner was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Ipswich School and Trinity College, Oxford. He served as Registrar, Honorary Librarian, and Principal at the University of the Punjab and its Oriental College.

Alfred Cort Haddon studied at King's College London and Christ's College, Cambridge. He held academic posts at the Royal College of Science for Ireland (1880–1901) and the University of Cambridge (1879–1880, 1900–1926).

Alfred Ernout was a linguist. He held academic posts at the University of Lille (1913–1924), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1924–1951), the University of Paris (~1927–1949), and the Collège de France (1941–1951).
Alfred Espinas was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and École Normale Supérieure. He held a post at the University of Paris from approximately 1893 to 1912.

Alfred Forke was a scholar of Sinology and philosophy who studied at the Universities of Geneva and Berlin. He held posts at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen, Humboldt University of Berlin, and the University of Hamburg.

Alfred Foucher worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the ENS and EPHE under Sylvain Lévi, later holding posts at EFEO, EPHE, Columbia University, Sorbonne University, and the Maison Franco-Japonaise.

Alfred Gell studied at the University of Cambridge under Edmund Leach and at the London School of Economics. He held academic posts at the University of Sussex, the Australian National University, and the London School of Economics.
